'''Goran Dragić''' (born 6 May 1986) is a Slovenian former professional [[basketball]] player. Nicknamed "'''the Dragon'''", he played professional basketball in Slovenia and Spain before entering the NBA in 2008. Dragić also played for the [[Phoenix Suns]], [[Miami Heat]], [[Houston Rockets]], [[Toronto Raptors]], [[Brooklyn Nets]], [[Chicago Bulls]] and the [[Milwaukee Bucks]]. He was an [[All-NBA Third Team]] selection and the [[NBA Most Improved Player Award|NBA Most Improved Player]] with the Suns in 2014. He was named an [[NBA All-Star]] for the first time in 2018 with Miami. 

Internationally, Dragić led the senior [[Slovenian national basketball team|Slovenian national team]] to its first [[FIBA EuroBasket]] title in [[EuroBasket 2017|2017]], while being named the [[FIBA EuroBasket MVP|MVP of the tournament]]. He is second in all-time points scored for the team and has played ninety games for his country.

==Professional career==

===Slovan (2004–2006)===
Dragić made his debut in 2003, at the age of 17, in the Slovenian minor league with [[KK Ilirija]]. After one year, Dragic transferred to the top-level [[Premier A Slovenian Basketball League|Slovenian Basketball League]] and [[NLB League|Adriatic League]] club [[KD Slovan|Slovan]] in 2004. 

===Murcia (2006–2007)===
After spending two years with Slovan, Dragic transferred to the [[Liga ACB|Spanish ACB League]] club [[Saski Baskonia]], who [[loan (sports)|loaned]] him to the Spanish club [[CB Murcia|Murcia]], in 2006.

===Olimpija (2007–2008)===
Dragić joined the Slovenian club [[KK Olimpija|Union Olimpija]] in 2007, and he played there during the 2007–08 season, winning the Slovenian League championship with the team.<ref name="DragicNBAIC">{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/player/201609/goran-dragic/bio|title=Goran Dragic|work=[[NBA.com]]|access-date=20 November 2020}}</ref>

===Phoenix Suns (2008–2011)===
Dragić entered the [[2008 NBA draft]], where he was selected in the second round, 45th overall, by the [[San Antonio Spurs]]. His draft rights were then traded to the [[Phoenix Suns]] in exchange for cash considerations in addition to the draft rights to [[Malik Hairston]], the 48th pick. After the Suns finished a deal with [[Saski Baskonia|TAU Ceramica]] (now known as Caja Laboral), with whom he was under contract, they officially signed him on 22 September 2008.<ref name="SeptemberSign">{{cite web|title=Suns Sign Goran Dragic | The Official Site Of The Phoenix Suns|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/news/sign_dragic_080825.html|access-date=1 March 2014|work=Nba.com}}</ref> The Suns hoped that he would take over the starting point guard position after [[Steve Nash]] relinquished it.<ref name=SeptemberSign/><ref name=DecemberArticle12>{{cite web|url=http://www.azcentral.com/sports/suns/articles/2008/12/11/20081211sunsdebut1212.html |title=New suns may play tonight |publisher=Azcentral.com |access-date=1 March 2014}}</ref> On 25 January 2010, Dragić scored a then career high 32 points, hitting 6 of 7 three-pointers in a losing effort against the Utah Jazz.<ref>{{cite web|author=Loren Jorgensen |url=https://www.deseret.com/2010/1/26/20366792/utah-jazz-little-known-dragic-enjoys-career-night-for-suns/ |title=Utah Jazz: Little-known Dragic enjoys career night for Suns |publisher=Deseret News |date=26 January 2010 |access-date=1 March 2014}}</ref>

On 7 May 2010, during [[2010 NBA Playoffs#(3) Phoenix Suns vs. (7) San Antonio Spurs|game 3 of the Western Conference Semifinals]], he led a Phoenix Suns comeback against the team that originally drafted him, the San Antonio Spurs, scoring 23 of his total 26 points in the fourth quarter. Dragić scored his points on 10/13 FG attempts including 5/5 three-pointers and a 4-point play, as the Suns overcame an early 18-point deficit to defeat the Spurs 110–96 and take a 3–0 lead in their best of seven series in the Western Conference Semifinals. "I think it's safe to say that may have been the best fourth-quarter performance I have ever seen in a playoff game", Suns forward [[Grant Hill]] said.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://scores.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=300507024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100510214929/http://scores.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=300507024 |url-status=dead |archive-date=10 May 2010 |title=Phoenix Suns vs. San Antonio Spurs - Recap - May 07, 2010 - ESPN |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=7 May 2010 |access-date=1 March 2014}}</ref>

===Houston Rockets (2011)===
On 24 February 2011, Dragić was traded to the [[Houston Rockets]] along with a protected first-round pick in exchange for [[Aaron Brooks (basketball)|Aaron Brooks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.azcentral.com/sports/suns/articles/2011/02/24/20110224phoenix-suns-goran-dragic-aaron-brooks-houston-rockets-nba-trade.html |title=Phoenix Suns trade Goran Dragic for Aaron Brooks from Houston Rockets |publisher=azcentral.com |access-date=25 August 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chron.com/sports/rockets/article/Rockets-trade-Battier-Brooks-in-separate-deals-1549128.php |title=Rockets trade Battier, Brooks in separate deals |work=Houston Chronicle |date=24 February 2011 |access-date=25 August 2011}}</ref> On 13 April 2011, in the Rockets' season finale, Dragić recorded his first career triple-double with 11 points, 11 assists and 11 rebounds in a 121–102 win over the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=310413016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170810170007/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=310413016|url-status=dead|archive-date=10 August 2017|title=Rockets send Timberwolves to 15th straight loss|work=ESPN.com|date=13 April 2011|access-date=29 March 2019}}</ref>

===Baskonia (2011)===
During the [[2011 NBA lockout]], Dragić played for [[Saski Baskonia]] of Spain.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/transactions/2011-12-signings/i/89886/5611/caja-laboral-tabs-guard-dragic |title=CAJA LABORAL tabs guard Dragic - 2011-12 SIGNINGS - Welcome to EUROLEAGUE BASKETBALL |publisher=Euroleague.net |date=20 November 2011 |access-date=1 March 2014}}</ref> He played for a brief period of time there until the lockout ended. 

===Return to Houston (2011–2012)===
Dragić returned to the Rockets for the 2011–12 season. Throughout most of the season, Dragić continued to be used as a bench player as a means to help the Rockets out during the lockout shortened season. In March 2012, he filled in for [[Kyle Lowry]], who was out with a bacterial infection. On 9 April 2012, Dragić won the Western Conference Player of the Week.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/2012/news/04/09/players-of-the-week-lebron-james-goran-dragic/ |title=Rockets' Dragic, Heat's James named Players of the Week |work=NBA.com |date=9 April 2012 |access-date=1 March 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140309150917/http://www.nba.com/2012/news/04/09/players-of-the-week-lebron-james-goran-dragic/ |archive-date=9 March 2014 }}</ref>

===Return to Phoenix (2012–2015)===
In 2012, Dragić became an unrestricted free agent. He agreed to sign a 4-year, $30 million deal with a player option on the final year with the [[Phoenix Suns]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.spotrac.com/nba/phoenix-suns/goran-dragic/ |title=Goran Dragic Salary Cap, Contracts, Salaries, Cap Hits, & News Profile |publisher=Spotrac.com |access-date=1 March 2014}}</ref> and officially became a member of the team again on 19 July 2012. He was brought in to replace [[Steve Nash]], whom he played behind during his first stint with the Suns, as starting point guard. On 19 February 2013, Dragić recorded a career-high 18 assists to go with 14 points as the Suns defeated the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] 102–98. Dragić nearly recorded a [[triple-double]] against the [[Brooklyn Nets]] with 31 points, 12 assists, and 9 rebounds on 24 March 2013. Despite suffering through a 25–57 season, Dragić ended up gaining some career high moments in the process.

After getting [[Eric Bledsoe]] from a trade with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]], the Suns ultimately decided to move Dragić to the shooting guard position as a means of putting less pressure on Dragić to distribute the ball to his teammates. In his first game playing with Bledsoe as a teammate, Dragić led the team with 26 points and 9 assists in a 104–91 season opening victory over the [[Portland Trail Blazers]]. Dragić had over 8 games with 30 points or more, including a double-double of 31 points and 10 assists in a victory against the Portland Trail Blazers on 27 November 2013. He also had what was, at the time, a career-high 33 points in a loss to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] on 2 January 2014. On 3 February 2014, Dragić won his second career Western Conference Player of the Week award and his first with the Suns for games played between 27 January – 2 February 2014.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/2014/news/02/03/lowry-dragic-named-players-of-week/index.html |title=Lowry, Dragic named Players of the Week |work=NBA.com |access-date=1 March 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140204162228/http://www.nba.com/2014/news/02/03/lowry-dragic-named-players-of-week/index.html |archive-date=4 February 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Three days later, he was paired with [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] guard [[Reggie Jackson (basketball, born 1990)|Reggie Jackson]] in the revamped, team-based Skills Challenge at the All-Star weekend

On 8 February 2014, Dragić scored a career-high 34 points— while attempting only 13 field-goals— to go along with 10 assists in a 122–109 home victory over the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140208/GSWPHX/gameinfo.html |title=Notebook: Suns 122, Warriors 109 |work=NBA.com |date=8 February 2014 |access-date=1 March 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180518132219/http://www.nba.com/games/20140208/GSWPHX/gameinfo.html |archive-date=18 May 2018 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On 23 February 2014, Dragić scored a new career-high 35 points, along with 3 assists and 3 steals, in a 112–115 loss to the Houston Rockets.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140223/HOUPHX/gameinfo.html |title=Notebook: Rockets 115, Suns 112 |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=1 March 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190526135405/https://www.nba.com/games/20140223/HOUPHX/gameinfo.html |archive-date=26 May 2019 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{YouTube|7jVMxL7-YPk|Goran Dragic Scores a Career-High 35 Points}}</ref> On 28 February 2014, he recorded a new career-high 40 points, along with 3 rebounds and 5 assists, in a 116–104 win over the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140228/NOPPHX/gameinfo.html |title=Notebook: Suns 116, Pelicans 104 |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=1 March 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190526140935/https://www.nba.com/games/20140228/NOPPHX/gameinfo.html |archive-date=26 May 2019 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{YouTube|Kp7ZqDY6vPg|Goran Dragic Scores a Career High... for the Second Time This Week!}}</ref> He became the first player, since [[Rod Strickland]] in 1985–86, to set career highs in points three times in a single month. Dragić also became the sixth player, after his head coach [[Jeff Hornacek]], [[Dražen Petrović]], [[Dirk Nowitzki]], [[LeBron James]], and [[Kevin Durant]], to join the 20-50-40 Club — averaging 20 or more points per game while shooting 50%+ from the field and 40%+ on three-pointers.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.brightsideofthesun.com/2014/4/7/5588628/phoenix-suns-goran-dragic-about-to-join-exclusive-20-50-40-club|title=Dragic could join Hornacek in 20/50/40 club|date=7 April 2014}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://valleyofthesuns.com/2014/04/16/goran-dragic-joins-hornacek-petrovic-on-exclusive-list/|title=Goran Dragic joins Hornacek, Petrovic on exclusive list|date=16 April 2014|access-date=22 April 2014|archive-date=1 October 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221001080816/https://valleyofthesuns.com/2014/04/16/goran-dragic-joins-hornacek-petrovic-on-exclusive-list/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He also averaged over 5 assists per game throughout the season as well, leaving him joining the likes of [[Larry Bird]], [[Jeff Hornacek]] and [[LeBron James]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.brightsideofthesun.com/2014/4/23/5643752/phoenix-suns-goran-dragic-named-nbas-most-improved-player-for-2013-14|title = Dragic is NBA's Most Improved Player|date = 23 April 2014}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.brightsideofthesun.com/2014/6/4/5779748/phoenix-suns-goran-dragic-named-to-2013-14-all-nba-third-team|title = Dragic selected to All-NBA Third Team|date = 4 June 2014}}</ref>

On 23 April 2014, Dragić won the 2014 [[NBA Most Improved Player Award]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/2014/news/04/23/goran-dragic-wins-kia-most-improved-player-award/ |title=Suns' Dragic wins Kia Most Improved Player award |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=23 April 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180128094023/http://www.nba.com/2014/news/04/23/goran-dragic-wins-kia-most-improved-player-award/ |archive-date=28 January 2018 |url-status=dead }}</ref> One month later, he would end up being honored by his home nation with their national "Apple of Inspiration" award for being a role model and inspiring hope in Slovenia, as well as helping out the nation's community with humanitarian activities.<ref>[http://www.sta.si/en/vest.php?s=a&id=2012201 Basketball Player Dragić Honoured by President Pahor]</ref> Finally, on 4 June 2014, Dragić was named to the 2014 [[All-NBA team|All-NBA Third Team]] alongside [[Damian Lillard]], [[LaMarcus Aldridge]], [[Al Jefferson]] and [[Paul George]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/2014/news/06/04/2013-14-all-nba-teams/ |title=Durant, LeBron headline 2013-14 All-NBA First Team |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=4 June 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140604220936/http://www.nba.com/2014/news/06/04/2013-14-all-nba-teams/ |archive-date=4 June 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Miami Heat (2015–2021)===

==== 2015–2017: First years in Miami ====
[[File:Goran Dragic (30303474504).jpg|thumb|Dragić with the Heat in 2016]]
On 19 February 2015, Dragić and his brother [[Zoran Dragić|Zoran Dragic]], were traded to the [[Miami Heat]] in a three-team deal also involving the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] that sent [[John Salmons]] and [[Danny Granger]] to Phoenix.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-acquire-goran-dragic-and-zoran-dragic|title=HEAT Acquire Goran Dragic and Zoran Dragic|date=19 February 2015|work=NBA.com|access-date=19 February 2015}}</ref> Two days later, he made his debut for the Heat, recording 12 points and 3 rebounds in a 105–91 loss to the New Orleans Pelicans.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150221/NOPMIA/gameinfo.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150223235430/http://www.nba.com/games/20150221/NOPMIA/gameinfo.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=23 February 2015|title=Pelicans lose Davis and Anderson, roll past Heat 105-91|date=21 February 2015|work=NBA.com|access-date=22 February 2015}}</ref> Dragić finished the season averaging 16.6 points and 5.3 assists per game in 26 starts for Miami, as the Heat missed the playoffs barely.

On 9 July 2015, Dragić re-signed with the Heat to a five-year, $90 million contract.<ref>{{cite news|title=HEAT Re-Signs Goran Dragic|url=http://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-re-signs-goran-dragic|access-date=13 July 2015|work=NBA.com|date=9 July 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | last = Stein | first = Marc | title = Goran Dragic, Miami Heat agree to five-year, $90 million deal | url = https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/13179887/goran-dragic-miami-heat-reach-agreement-five-year-90-million-deal | work = ESPN.com | date = 1 July 2015 | access-date = 1 July 2015}}</ref> In January 2016, he missed eight straight games because of a left calf injury.<ref>{{cite web | last = Braun | first = Rick | title = Miami Heat guard Goran Dragic likely to return Friday night vs. Bucks | url = http://www.miamiherald.com/sports/nba/miami-heat/article57195813.html | work = MiamiHerald.com | date = 28 January 2016 | access-date = 30 January 2016}}</ref> On 20 February 2016, he recorded a season-high 24 points, eight assists and seven rebounds in a 114–84 win over the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Whiteside has 25 points, 23 rebounds; Heat beat Wizards|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160220/WASMIA/gameinfo.html|access-date=21 February 2016|work=NBA.com|date=20 February 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170209230443/http://www.nba.com/games/20160220/WASMIA/gameinfo.html|archive-date=9 February 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> He bested that season high on 11 March, recording 26 points and nine assists in a 118–96 win over the [[Chicago Bulls]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Dragic scores 26 as Heat beat Bulls 118-96|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160311/MIACHI/gameinfo.html|access-date=11 March 2016|work=NBA.com|date=11 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170108011007/http://www.nba.com/games/20160311/MIACHI/gameinfo.html|archive-date=8 January 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 7 April, he recorded 16 points and a career-high 12 rebounds in a 106–98 win over the Chicago Bulls, helping the Heat sweep the season series with the Bulls for the first time since the 2003–04 season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Heat rally past Bulls, 106-98 for 46th win of the season|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160407/CHIMIA/gameinfo.html|access-date=7 April 2016|work=NBA.com|date=7 April 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181209124735/http://www.nba.com/games/20160407/CHIMIA/gameinfo.html|archive-date=9 December 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> In the Heat's second-round playoff match-up with the Toronto Raptors, Dragić scored a postseason career-high 30 points to help the Heat to a 103–91 victory in Game 6, tying the series at 3–3.<ref>{{cite news|title=Dragic, Wade lead Heat past Raptors 103-91 _ and into Game 7|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160513/TORMIA/gameinfo.html|access-date=14 May 2016|work=NBA.com|date=13 May 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181209124900/http://www.nba.com/games/20160513/TORMIA/gameinfo.html|archive-date=9 December 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> The Heat went on to lose Game 7, bowing out of the playoffs with a 4–3 defeat.

On 28 November 2016, Dragić recorded season highs of 27 points and 17 assists in a 112–104 loss to the Boston Celtics.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899706|title=Thomas scores 25, Celtics get past Heat 112-104|work=ESPN.com|date=28 November 2016|access-date=29 November 2016}}</ref> He topped that mark on 6 December 2016, scoring 29 points (his highest-scoring total as a member of the Heat at the time) in a 114–103 loss to the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899758|title=Anthony scores 35, Knicks beat depleted Heat 114-103|work=ESPN.com|date=6 December 2016|access-date=6 December 2016}}</ref> Dragić set a new season high six days later, scoring 34 points in a 112–101 win over the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899805|title=Dragic scores 34, Heat beat Wizards 112-101 to snap slide|work=ESPN.com|date=12 December 2016|access-date=12 December 2016}}</ref> On 6 February 2017, he scored 33 points and hit a career-high seven three-pointers to lead the Heat to their 11th straight victory with a 115–113 win over the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900180|title=Dragic leads Heat to 11th straight win, 115-113 over Wolves|work=ESPN.com|date=6 February 2017|access-date=7 February 2017}}</ref>

==== 2017–2021: All-Star and Finals appearance ====
On 8 November 2017, Dragić scored a season-high 29 points in a 126–115 win over the Phoenix Suns.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974913|title=Goran Dragic scores season-high 29, Heat beat Suns 126-115|work=ESPN.com|date=8 November 2017|access-date=8 November 2017}}</ref> On 27 November 2017, he was named the Eastern Conference Player of the Week for games played 20 November through 26 November.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/heat/news/goran-dragic-named-eastern-conference-player-week|title=Goran Dragic Named Eastern Conference Player of the Week|work=NBA.com|date=27 November 2017|access-date=28 November 2017}}</ref> On 15 January 2018, he was named the Eastern Conference Player of the Week for games played 8 January through 14 January. It was his fourth career Player of the Week honor.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/heat/news/goran-dragic-named-eastern-conference-player-week-0|title=Goran Dragić Named Eastern Conference Player Of The Week|work=NBA.com|date=15 January 2018|access-date=15 January 2018}}</ref> On 1 February, Dragić was named the replacement for [[Kevin Love]] on Team [[LeBron James|LeBron]] for the [[2018 NBA All-Star Game]], thus making him an All-Star for the first time in his career.<ref>{{cite news|title=Dragic Selected to 2018 NBA All-Star Team|url=http://www.nba.com/heat/dragic-selected-to-2018-nba-all-star-team|access-date=1 February 2018|work=NBA.com|date=1 February 2018}}</ref>

On 27 October 2018, Dragić scored 28 points in a 120–111 win over the [[Portland Trail Blazers]], becoming the first [[Slovenia]]n player to reach the 10,000-point mark in the NBA.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070760|title=Dragic scores 28, Heat outlast Trail Blazers 120-111|work=ESPN.com|date=27 October 2018|access-date=27 October 2018}}</ref> In late November and early December, he missed eight games with a sore right knee.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071057|title=Adebayo's career-high 22 points helps Heat beat Suns 115-98|work=ESPN.com|date=7 December 2018|access-date=8 December 2018}}</ref> On 19 December, he underwent successful surgery to clean up his right knee.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/goran-dragic-undergoes-surgery-181219|title=Goran Dragić Undergoes Surgery|work=NBA.com|date=19 December 2018|access-date=19 December 2018}}</ref> He returned to action on 23 February 2019 against the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071561|title=Pistons reach 7th in East, top reeling Heat 119-96|work=ESPN.com|date=23 February 2018|access-date=24 February 2018|quote=Miami got point guard Goran Dragic on the floor for the first time since Dec. 10, after a two-month rehab to recover from right knee surgery.}}</ref> On 28 March, he recorded his second career triple-double with 23 points, 12 rebounds and 11 assists in a 105–99 win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071797|title=Dragic's triple-double lifts Heat past Mavs, 105-99|work=ESPN.com|date=28 March 2019|access-date=29 March 2019}}</ref>

In the [[2019–20 NBA season]], Dragić helped the Heat through the [[2020 NBA Playoffs]]. In Game 1 of the Eastern Conference Finals, Dragic scored a team-leading 29 points during a 117–114 overtime win over the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20220419160018/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401245393 Bam Adebayo's block helps Heat win Game 1 over Celtics]</ref> After winning that series, in the [[2020 NBA Finals]] they faced the [[Los Angeles Lakers]]. Dragić missed 4 games in the Finals due to a plantar fasciitis injury that he suffered in Game 1. The Heat lost the series in six games.

On 30 December 2020, Dragić scored a season-high 26 points, alongside five rebounds and two assists, in a 119–108 win over the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=HEAT AVENGE EMBARRASSMENT, RALLY TO TOP BUCKS 119-108 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022000058 |access-date=27 February 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On 26 February 2021, he scored 26 points, alongside three rebounds, two assists and two steals, in a 124–116 win over the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=BUTLER, DRAGIC CARRY HEAT PAST NBA-BEST JAZZ, 124-116 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022000507 |access-date=27 February 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> During the first round of the playoffs, the Heat faced the Bucks. On 22 May, Dragić recorded 25 points and two rebounds in a 109–107 Game 1 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=KHRIS MIDDLETON LIFTS BUCKS PAST HEAT IN OT IN GAME 1 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0042000121 |access-date=27 February 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

===Toronto Raptors (2021–2022)===
On 6 August 2021, the [[Toronto Raptors]] acquired Dragić and [[Precious Achiuwa]] from the Heat via a sign-and-trade in exchange for [[Kyle Lowry]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-acquire-kyle-lowry|title=HEAT ACQUIRE KYLE LOWRY|work=NBA.com|date=6 August 2021}}</ref> Shortly after being acquired by the Raptors, Dragić gave an interview in his native Slovenia where he reportedly stated that he did not want to play for the team and that he had "higher ambitions;" he would apologize shortly after for his comments<ref>{{Cite web|first=Michael |last=Grange |title=Dragic determined to make things right after comments about Raptors future|url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nba/article/dragic-determined-make-things-right-comments-raptors-future/ |date=10 August 2021 |access-date=2 July 2026|website=[[Sportsnet]]|language=en}}</ref> and ultimately suit up to start the season with Toronto.

On 28 November, Dragić announced he was stepping away from the Raptors for personal reasons.<ref>{{Cite web|author=The Athletic Staff|title=Raptors' Goran Dragic out indefinitely for personal reasons|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3687653/2021/11/28/raptors-goran-dragic-out-indefinitely-for-personal-reasons/|access-date=21 December 2021|website=The Athletic|language=en}}</ref> On 10 February 2022, Dragić and a 2022 first-round pick were traded to the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in exchange for [[Drew Eubanks]], [[Thaddeus Young]] and a 2022 second-round pick.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/spurs-acquire-goran-dragic-2022-first-round-pick|title=SPURS ACQUIRE GORAN DRAGIĆ & 2022 FIRST ROUND PICK|work=NBA.com|date=10 February 2022}}</ref> He and the Spurs agreed to a contract buyout five days later.<ref>{{Cite magazine|title=Report: Goran Dragić, Spurs Agree to Buyout As Point Guard Enters Free Agency|url=https://www.si.com/nba/2022/02/15/goran-dragic-spurs-agree-contract-buyout-free-agency|access-date=16 February 2022|magazine=Sports Illustrated}}</ref>

===Brooklyn Nets (2022)===
On 22 February 2022, Dragić signed with the [[Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Goran Dragić |url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2022/02/22/brooklyn-nets-sign-goran-dragic |website=NBA.com |access-date=5 July 2022 |date=22 February 2022}}</ref> He made his Nets debut four days later, recording six points, three rebounds and two assists in a 126–123 win over the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=IRVING HAS SEASON-HIGH 38, NETS RALLY TO BEAT BUCKS 126-123 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022100910 |access-date=27 February 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On 16 March, Dragić scored a season-high 21 points, alongside three rebounds and four assists, in a 113–111 loss to the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=DINWIDDIE HITS 3 AT BUZZER, MAVERICKS BEAT NETS 113-111 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022101036 |access-date=27 February 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> The Nets faced the [[Boston Celtics]] during the first round of the playoffs, but were eliminated in a four-game sweep.

===Chicago Bulls (2022–2023)===
On 2 August 2022, Dragić signed with the [[Chicago Bulls]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Bulls sign Goran Dragić |url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-goran-dragic |website=NBA.com |access-date=3 August 2022 |date=2 August 2022}}</ref> On 28 February 2023, he was waived by the Bulls.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bulls waive Dragić |url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-waive-dragic |access-date=28 February 2023 |website=NBA}}</ref>

===Milwaukee Bucks (2023)===
On 4 March 2023, Dragić signed with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Milwaukee Bucks Sign Goran Dragić|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-sign-goran-dragic|website=NBA.com|date=4 March 2023|access-date=4 March 2023}}</ref>

On 31 December 2023, Dragić announced his retirement from professional basketball.<ref>{{cite web|first=Tim|last=Reynolds|url=https://www.nba.com/news/goran-dragic-retires-from-nba|title=Goran Dragic announces his retirement after a 15-year NBA career|website=NBA.com|date=31 December 2023|access-date=31 December 2023}}</ref>

==National team career==

===Slovenian junior national team===
Dragić won the gold medal at the [[2004 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship]] with the [[Slovenia men's national under-20 basketball team|Slovenian under-20 junior national team]]. He also played at the [[2005 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship]].

===Slovenian senior national team===
[[File:Slovenia vs. Serbia at EuroBasket 2009 (36).jpg|thumb|Dragić playing with [[Slovenian national basketball team|Slovenia]] at the [[2009 EuroBasket]]]]
Dragić competed with the senior men's [[Slovenia national basketball team|Slovenian national basketball team]] at the [[2006 FIBA World Championship]] and the [[2007 EuroBasket]], in limited roles. Dragić's role with the Slovenian national basketball team began to increase in the [[2009 EuroBasket]] and the [[2010 FIBA World Championship]]. He then played with his brother [[Zoran Dragić|Zoran]] in the [[2011 EuroBasket]] and the [[2013 EuroBasket]], the latter which was held in [[Slovenia]]. During the 2013 tournament, Goran and his brother helped lead Slovenia to a 5th-place finish and a spot in the [[2014 FIBA World Cup]]. Dragić finished in the 2013 EuroBasket's top five in points and assists, which earned him a spot on the [[EuroBasket All-Tournament Team|All-Tournament Team]]. In 2014, Dragić was named Slovenia's [[captain (sports)|team captain]] after [[Jaka Lakovič]] retired from [[national sports team|national team]] play. In the [[friendly game]]s before the [[2014 FIBA World Cup]], Dragić was rested in 9 of their 14 games, before actually playing in the official tournament's matches. After finishing up their friendly games, Dragić played with no restrictions beyond the rest of the competition; he was the only [[All-NBA Team]] member to play in the 2014 FIBA World Cup, aside from the [[2014 United States FIBA Basketball World Cup team|Team USA]] members.{{citation needed|date=January 2015}}

Prior to the [[2017 EuroBasket]], Dragić announced that he would retire from playing with the Slovenian national team after the tournament.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/miami-heat/fl-sp-miami-heat-goran-dragic-s20170829-story.html |title=Miami Heat guard Goran Dragic to retire from international play after EuroBasket |first=Ira |last=Winderman |newspaper=[[Sun-Sentinel]] |location=[[Deerfield Beach, Florida]] |date=29 August 2017 |access-date=19 September 2017}}</ref> At the tournament, he helped Slovenia to win its first ever FIBA European championship. He scored 35 points, on 12-22 shooting in the [[EuroBasket 2017 Final|final]], which was the most points scored in a final, since [[Pau Gasol]] scored 36 points in the [[EuroBasket 2003|2003]] final.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://heatzone.blog.palmbeachpost.com/2017/09/17/goran-dragic-leads-slovenia-to-eurobasket-gold-with-35-points-named-mvp-of-tournament/|title=Goran Dragic leads Slovenia to EuroBasket gold with 35 points - Heat Zone|archive-date=18 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170918025457/http://heatzone.blog.palmbeachpost.com/2017/09/17/goran-dragic-leads-slovenia-to-eurobasket-gold-with-35-points-named-mvp-of-tournament/|access-date=22 July 2019}}</ref> Following his performance, Dragić was given the [[FIBA EuroBasket MVP|Most Valuable Player award of the tournament]], after averaging 22.6 points per game, in 9 games played.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/eurobasket/2017/news/title-hero-dragic-caps-off-fairy-tale-finish-with-mvp-honors|title=Title hero Dragic caps off fairy tale finish with MVP honors|website=FIBA.basketball|date=17 September 2017 |language=en|access-date=19 September 2017}}</ref><ref name=MVP>{{cite web|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/eurobasket/2017/news/title-hero-dragic-caps-off-fairy-tale-finish-with-mvp-honors|title=Title hero Dragic caps off fairy tale finish with MVP honors|publisher=fiba.basketball|date=17 September 2017}}</ref> Following that performance, he was named the 2017 [[Slovenian Sportsman of the year]].

Five years later, in June 2022, Dragić returned to the Slovenian team to play in the third window of the [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup qualification (Europe)|qualification]] for the [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=It's official: Dragic comes out of retirement to join Doncic in Slovenia's 15 |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2023/european-qualifiers/news/it-s-official-dragic-comes-out-of-retirement-joins-doncic-in-slovenia-s-15 |access-date=5 July 2022 |website=FIBA.basketball |date=6 June 2022 |language=en}}</ref> On 30 June, he scored 19 points in his first game back, helping his country to a blowout win over [[Croatia men's national basketball team|Croatia]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=FIBA Basketball World Cup 2023 European Qualifiers |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2023/european-qualifiers/player/Goran-Dragic |access-date=5 July 2022 |website=FIBA.basketball |language=en}}</ref>

Dragić also played at [[EuroBasket 2022]], averaging 14.9 points on 49.4% shooting as the team's sixth man.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Goran DRAGIC at the FIBA EuroBasket 2022 |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/eurobasket/2022/player/Goran-Dragic |access-date=16 September 2022 |website=FIBA.basketball |language=en}}</ref> Slovenia was surprisingly eliminated by Poland in the quarter-finals.

Dragić was Slovenia's all-time scoring leader with 1,050 points in his 90 games,<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Dragon |url=https://www.goran-dragic.com/the-dragon/ |access-date=2025-09-05 |website=Goran Dragić Foundation |language=en-US}}</ref> before being surpassed by [[Luka Doncic]] on 4 September 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-09-04 |title=Luka Magic is real: Doncic near triple-double conjures Slovenia victory |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/events/fiba-eurobasket-2025/news/luka-magic-is-real-doncic-near-triple-double-conjures-slovenia-victory |access-date=2025-09-05 |website=www.fiba.basketball |language=en}}</ref>

His jersey number 3 was retired by the [[Basketball Federation of Slovenia]] on 23 August 2024, ahead of his farewell game at the [[Arena Stožice]] in [[Ljubljana]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Goran Dragic No. 3 jersey retired by Slovenia |url=https://basketnews.com/news-210846-.html#:~:text=Slovenian%20Basketball%20Federation%20(KZS)%20announced,able%20to%20select%20this%20number.&text=Ahead%20of%20his%20farewell%20game,Slovenian%20Basketball%20Federation%20(KZS). |access-date=2024-08-24 |website=basketnews.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=FAQ: Goran Dragic caps career with 'Night of the Dragon' |url=https://www.nba.com/news/faq-goran-dragic-night-of-the-dragon |access-date=2024-08-24 |website=NBA.com |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Dragić was born to a Slovenian mother and a [[Serbs|Serbian]] father.<ref>[http://www.downtownphoenixjournal.com/2010/02/04/suns-spot-el-dragon/]  {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100302192458/http://www.downtownphoenixjournal.com/2010/02/04/suns-spot-el-dragon/|date=2 March 2010}}</ref> He grew up in Slovenia playing [[Association football|football]]. However, an injury forced him to switch sports. As a child, he admired NBA players [[Michael Jordan]], [[Allen Iverson]] and future teammate [[Steve Nash]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/goran_dragic/bio.html|title=Goran Dragic Stats, Video, Bio, Profile|work=NBA.com|access-date=1 March 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131025071832/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/goran_dragic/bio.html|archive-date=25 October 2013}}</ref> He is fluent in [[Slovene language|Slovene]], [[Serbian language|Serbian]], [[Spanish language|Spanish]], and English.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://nba.us/playerfile/goran_dragic/bio.html |title=Goran Dragic Stats, Video, Bio, Profile | NBA.com |publisher=Nba.us |access-date=1 March 2014}}</ref> Dragić's younger brother, [[Zoran Dragić|Zoran]], was formerly his teammate on the Phoenix Suns and Miami Heat.<ref>{{cite news|title=Suns Sign Zoran Dragić|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-sign-zoran-dragic|date=29 September 2014|access-date=30 September 2014|work=NBA.com}}</ref>

Dragić has two children with his ex-wife.<ref>{{cite web |title=Goran Dragic apologizes for saying he has 'higher ambitions' than Raptors after trade from Miami |url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/basketball/nba/goran-dragic-comments-raptors-trade-heat-1.6136129 |website=CBC.ca |access-date=21 February 2022 |date=10 August 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=3 September 2021 |title=Goran Dragić se ločuje |url=https://www.24ur.com/popin/domaca-scena/goran-dragic-se-locuje.html |access-date=28 February 2024 |website=24ur.com}}</ref>

He and Zoran, alongside teammates [[Markieff Morris|Markieff]] and [[Marcus Morris (basketball)|Marcus Morris]], all briefly played together for the Suns during the fourth quarter of their 112–96 victory over the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] on 2 January 2015. It marked the first time in the NBA's history that two different pairs of brothers played together for the same team at the same time.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150102/PHIPHX/gameinfo.html |title=Green helps Suns pull away from 76ers, 112-96 |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=9 January 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170901084149/http://www.nba.com/games/20150102/PHIPHX/gameinfo.html |archive-date=1 September 2017 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

[[President of Republika Srpska]] [[Milorad Dodik]] honored Dragić with an Order of Njegoš and a Medal of Merit for the People, in August 2018.<ref>{{cite web |title=Goran Dragić posetio Igokeu, Dodik ga odlikovao Njegoševim ordenom |url=https://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2018&mm=08&dd=15&nav_id=1431133 |website=b92.net | date=15 August 2018 |access-date=16 August 2018}}</ref>

Dragić is a [[Serbian Orthodox Church|Serbian Orthodox Christian]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Sem Slovenec , pravoslavne vere. Na današnji praznik ti želim, mir v duši in radost v srcu. |url=https://twitter.com/Goran_Dragic/status/1082307839467708416 |website=twitter.com |access-date=7 January 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=МИР БОЖИЈИ, ХРИСТОС СЕ РОДИ! |url=https://twitter.com/reno_968/status/1082306420123545600 |website=twitter.com |access-date=7 January 2019}}</ref>
